newsitem.title: UK: RALLYING-DOMINANT SCHWARZ WINS BRITISH RAC RALLY IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-DOMINANT SCHWARZ WINS BRITISH RAC RALLY IN STYLE.

text.p: Armin Schwarz of Germany drove to a convincing victory in the British RAC Rally on Monday when he brought his Toyota home nearly eight minutes clear of Japan's Masao Kaimoka in a Subaru.

Schwarz, who led the rally from the first stage to the last, was seven minutes 52 seconds clear after the final stage at the end of the third day of a rally overshadowed by accidents and retirements in treacherous conditions.
Veteran Swede Stig Blomqvist finished third in a Skoda on the Czech manufacturers' 25th appearance in the RAC rally which this year was not a world championship event.
Briton Mark Higgins finished fourth in a Nissan.

Schwarz's winning margin was the biggest since Blomqvist won the RAC for the second time in 1983 and was also his second major rally victory. His only world championship win came at the Catalonia Rally of 1991.
Forrmula One driver Martin Brundle, making his rallying debut in a Ford Escort, did not finish. He left the road on the first stage of the day and was forced to retire after the turbo caught fire.

Brundle said of his crash: "It feels very sad that it came to grief when it all seemed under control. I probably made the classic rallying mistake of losing concentration while unsighted behind another car."
